name: desyncsmith
concept: An end-to-end request-smuggling lab tool: it fingerprints the lab's proxy<->origin pair, replays CL.TE / TE.CL / TE.TE differential probe batteries with latency-orthogonality scoring plus mitigation control runs against a known-patched control proxy, then lets the operator mount a weaponization chain — cache poisoning, front-end auth bypass, or stored-XSS admin-session poisoning — entirely inside the allowlisted lab. Ships multi-repetition significance scoring and patched-control validation gates instead of single-shot 'vulnerable' judgments.
attack_vectors: CL.TE / TE.CL / TE.TE differential detection with timing-orthogonality + teardown-analysis scoring
Cache poisoning of a cacheable lab resource via smuggled request reshaping origin responses
Front-end auth bypass where FE logs a benign request while the origin executes a privileged one
Admin-session / stored-XSS poisoning via cross-user request interleaving
Mitigation validation gate: findings accepted only when patched-control proxy stays clean across the same probe set
novelty_angle: Prior request-smuggling tooling mostly stops at detection or one-off PoCs; this couples detection with a repeatable exploit-chain decision engine and, unusually, bakes in a mitigation-validation control arm so false positives on flaky technique are measured, not assumed.
dependencies: Python 3.10+ stdlib (ipaddress, http.client, socket, ssl, subprocess)
docker-compose lab: nginx/Varnish front + gunicorn/Flask origin + patched control proxy
optional httpx only if stdlib probing proves too slow
raw bytesmithing for exact CL/TE framing (no library leakage of Host/Content-Length)
scope_gate: ipaddress resolver gate re-checked before every probe: each resolved host (front AND origin AND controls) must be loopback (127.0.0.0/8, ::1) or RFC1918 or inside user-supplied lab CIDR; any out-of-allowlist resolution hard-refuses with WARN banner on first run; DNS-rebinding guard re-resolves and re-validates per probe.
